title.en: AI Can Generate, but Humans Create

narrative_brief: Mini PechaKucha for Science Communication (SDG 9 × AI Literacy × Science Communication)

A2.text: Good morning. Today we look at SDG 9, a global plan from the United Nations. It asks every country to back new technology and to build stronger systems.
A2.authored_by: Claude (English teacher role), v2 against the v2 quality gate
A2.basis: Written from scratch, not edited from the workbook. The three workbook levels of this mission shared 0.57 of their vocabulary at both level boundaries, which means A2, B1 and B2 were one text with a few words swapped, and every A2 slide failed the band - one 32-word sentence per slide, a semicolon in the middle of it, and a Flesch-Kincaid grade far above A2. This A2 is short spoken sentences, one idea each, with because-clauses on slides 4 and 5 for the A2 subordinator and no participle clauses: the workbook's '..., meaning that...' and '..., doubting old ideas, and sharing...' are all above A2 and have been rewritten as finite clauses. A2.workbook_text: As future scientists, we must continue asking good questions, doubting old ideas, and sharing our discoveries honestly, because these special human abilities will always be necessary no matter how smart computers become.

title.en: The Human Edge: Redefining the human role

A2.text: SDG 9 reminds us that people drive every new idea. A machine can hand us facts. But only a person can turn facts into real knowledge.

A2.workbook_text: In conclusion, SDG 9 reminds us that innovation is always driven by people, because AI can give us basic information, but only human beings can create true knowledge and make the right choices.

title.en: Final Call to Action: The SDG 9 future vision

A2.text: So let's use AI wisely. Keep your wonder, your new ideas and your honest heart. Those three habits really make a scientist, and they build a better future.
